ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.claim: Every part of Sūrah al-Zukhruf relates deeply to its central theme, and the whole sūrah forms a harmonious unit from beginning to end.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.anchor: each part of it is deeply related to its central theme

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r15.claim: The riders' declaration means they will return to God and affirms resurrection; travel by ship or mount risks drowning or a fall, so riders should remain ready to meet God in heart and speech.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r15.anchor: وإنا إلى ربنا لمنقلبون: أي راجعون، وهو إقرار بالرجوع إلى الله، وبالبعث،

STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r7.claim: The surah challenges the worldview of the Makkan idolaters, answering their objections and addressing forms of disbelief.
STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r7.anchor: The first half of the sūrah responds to different objections that the Makkan idolaters are reported to have posed to the message of the Quran

NAHHAS:v4p100/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p100/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p100/r3.claim: The statement is coordinated with the preceding speech.
NAHHAS:v4p100/r3.anchor: معطوف على ما قبله من القول

ZAJJAJ:v4p406/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p406/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p406/r6.claim: The statement is an acknowledgment that people will be resurrected.

IBNHIBBAN:2697/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:2697/r1.speaker: علي بن ربيعة الأسدي
IBNHIBBAN:2697/r1.claim: ʿAlī b. Rabīʿa recounts that ʿAlī invoked God while mounting, praised His provision and subjection of transport, recited 43:13–14, said takbīr three times and sought forgiveness; he adds that the Prophet did likewise while he rode behind him.
IBNHIBBAN:2697/r1.anchor: عن علي بن ربيعة الأسدي، قال: ركب علي دابة

ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r12.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r12.claim: A report from Ali, graded authentic by al-Tirmidhi, gives the mounting supplication: say ‘in God’s name’ at the stirrup, praise and magnify God three times, recite the verses, then seek forgiveness; Ali says the Prophet did likewise and describes God’s delight at the plea.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r12.anchor: وأخرج أحمد وأبو داود والترمذي وصححه والنسائي وجماعة عن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه

ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r13.speaker: ابن عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r13.claim: A report in Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, Abu Dawud, and al-Darimi says the Prophet praised, glorified, and magnified God three times when mounting his camel to travel, then recited these verses. No grading is stated here.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r13.anchor: وفي حديث أخرجه مسلم والترمذي وأبو داود والدارمي عن ابن عمر أن رسول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v25p69#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p69#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p69#2/r1.claim: ‘We will return’ means returning to God; a rider should make travel a reminder of the greater return, order conduct by that awareness, and ride only for a lawful purpose because riding is perilous.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p69#2/r1.anchor: وفيه إيذان بأن حق الراكب أن يتأمل فيما يلابسه من السير ويتذكر منه المسافرة العظمى

TIRMIDHI:3447/r1.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:3447/r1.speaker: النبي
TIRMIDHI:3447/r1.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that the Prophet recited this verse and 43:14 when mounting for travel, then prayed for piety, accepted deeds, an easier journey, and protection for companions and family; Tirmidhi grades the report ḥasan gharīb from this route.
TIRMIDHI:3447/r1.anchor: أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم كَانَ إِذَا سَافَرَ فَرَكِبَ رَاحِلَتَهُ كَبَّرَ ثَلاَثًا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207#2/r7.claim: People return to their Lord at the resurrection.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207#2/r7.anchor: {وإنا إلى ربنا لمنقلبون} لمنصرفون في المعاد.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207#2/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207#2/r8.claim: Ali ibn Rabia saw Ali recite the mounted supplication, praise and magnify God, seek forgiveness, and laugh; Ali said the Prophet did likewise and marveled at a servant who knows only God forgives sins.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207#2/r8.anchor: رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم 117/ب فعل ما فعلت، وقال مثل ما قلت، ثم ضحك، فقلنا: ما يضحكك يا نبي الله؟ قال: "العبد"

BAYDAWI-FULL:43:13-14/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:13-14/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:13-14/r1.claim: منقلبون means that the riders will return to God.
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:13-14/r1.anchor: وإنا إلى ربنا لمنقلبون } أي راجعون

BAYDAWI-FULL:43:13-14/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:13-14/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:13-14/r2.claim: The return completes the travel imagery: riding entails movement, whose greatest journey is the return to God; alternatively, travel reminds riders of death and to prepare for meeting God.
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:13-14/r2.anchor: واتصاله بذلك لأن الركوب للتنقل والنقلة العظمى

BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r1.claim: People travel on the earth as on a ship or animal through time and its changing events, often forgetting that they are on a journey and at risk of death.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r1.anchor: ظهر هذه الأرض لهم مثل ظهور السفن والدواب يسبحون بها في لجج أمواج الزمان وتصاريف الحدثان

BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r2.claim: منقلبون means heading toward and arriving at the afterlife through death, with no return to this world; earthly travel signals the journey after death.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r3.claim: The statement is emphatic because the audience denies resurrection, and keeps riders mindful of the Benefactor as they travel toward him.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r3.anchor: وأكد لأجل إنكارهم للبعث حتى لا يزالوا مراقبين للمنعم عليهم

BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r4.claim: Alternatively, because riders were told to remember the blessing while traveling, the phrase recalls God’s gifts during repose before departure and after return: people are always in his favor.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المعنى أنه لما أمرهم بالمراقبة على نعمة الركوب

BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r5.speaker: علي
BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r5.claim: Ali’s report says that on mounting he said Bismillah, then praised God for subjecting the mount, praised and magnified God three times, and sought pardon; the author cites the Tirmidhi grading hasan sahih.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r5.anchor: عن علي رضي الله عنه أنه وضع رجله في الركاب وقال : بسم الله

BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r6.claim: In Ali’s report, the Prophet did likewise and said God marvels at the servant who asks pardon, knowing that only God forgives sins.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r6.anchor: وأخبر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فعل مثله

BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet rode with him, recited takbir, praise, and glorification three times each, then tahlil once, leaned back, and laughed; he described God’s smiling response to a rider who does likewise.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أردفه على دابة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r8.speaker: ابن عمر
BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r8.claim: Ibn Umar reports that the Prophet said the riding glorification and then prayed for righteousness and piety, accepted deeds, an easy journey, and care for his family; the cited collections are Ahmad, Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa’i, and al-Tirmidhi.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r8.anchor: وروى أحمد ومسلم وأبو داود والنسائي والترمذي عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا ركب راحلته

DURR-FULL:v7p368/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p368/r1.speaker: علي
DURR-FULL:v7p368/r1.claim: ʿAlī reports mounting with God's name, praising and magnifying Him, reciting both verses, and asking forgiveness; he had seen the Prophet do likewise.
DURR-FULL:v7p368/r1.anchor: عن علي رضي الله عنه أنه أتى بدابة فلما وضع رجله في الركاب قال: بسم الله فلما استوى على ظهرها

DURR-FULL:v7p368/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p368/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v7p368/r2.claim: The Prophet says God marvels at a servant asking forgiveness, knowing only God forgives sins.
DURR-FULL:v7p368/r2.anchor: فقلت يا رسول الله: مم ضحكت فقال: يعجب الرب من عبده إذا قال: رب اغفر لي

DURR-FULL:v7p368/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p368/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p368/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports the Prophet magnifying God three times and declaring His unity after settling on the mount, then laughing.
DURR-FULL:v7p368/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أردفه على دابته فلما استوى عليها (كبر ثلاثا

DURR-FULL:v7p369/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p369/r1.speaker: أبو مجلز
DURR-FULL:v7p369/r1.claim: Abū Mujliz says Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī taught a rider first to praise God for Islam, Muḥammad, and making the community best for humanity, then recite these verses.
DURR-FULL:v7p369/r1.anchor: عن أبي مجلز رضي الله عنه قال: رأى حسين بن علي رضي الله عنه رجلا يركب دابة فقال {سبحان الذي سخر لنا هذا

DURR-FULL:v7p369/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p369/r2.speaker: طاوس
DURR-FULL:v7p369/r2.claim: Ṭāwūs thanked God for the gift and bounty of the ride and recited both verses when mounting.
DURR-FULL:v7p369/r2.anchor: عن طاوس رضي الله عنه أنه كان إذ ركب دابة قال: بسم الله اللهم هذا من منك وفضلك علينا فلك الحمد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p174/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p174/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p174/r7.claim: The traveler's closing acknowledgment of return to God means return after death for resurrection, reckoning, and recompense, embedding belief in resurrection in the thanks.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p174/r7.anchor: أي بعد الموت بالبعث للحساب والجزاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p174/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p174/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p174/r8.claim: The return to God also alludes to a traveler's return home: the God who restores the dead to life can bring a traveler safely to family.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p174/r8.anchor: وفيه تعريض بسؤال إرجاع المسافر إلى أهله فإن الذي يقدر على إرجاع الأموات

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p48/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p48/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p48/r1.claim: The return declaration commands acknowledgment and repeated recollection of resurrection, prompting reflection on it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p48/r1.anchor: وقوله: وإنا إلى ربنا لمنقلبون أمر بالإقرار بالبعث وترداد القول به، وذلك داعية إلى استشعار النظر فيه،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p48/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p48/r2.speaker: النبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p48/r2.claim: A report says that if a rider omits this verse, Satan tells him to sing, or, if unable, to indulge fantasies and waste the time.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p48/r2.anchor: وروي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن الإنسان إذا ركب ولم يقل هذه الآية جاءه الشيطان فقال: «تغنه،

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p304#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p304#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p304#3/r1.claim: People will return to their Lord in the afterlife.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p220/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p220/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p220/r1.claim: Returning to God means coming to Him after death; worldly travel alerts people to the greater journey of the afterlife, as worldly provisions and clothing point to piety.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p220/r1.anchor: وهذا من باب التنبيه بسير الدنيا على سير الآخرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p220/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p220/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p220/r2.claim: Ali reports his mounting praise and supplication, then the Prophet's similar practice and teaching that God knows only He forgives sins; Tirmidhi grades it hasan sahih, with variant transmission routes noted.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p220/r2.anchor: حديث أمير المؤمنين علي بن أبي طالب، رضي الله عنه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p221/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p221/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p221/r2.claim: Ibn Umar reports the Prophet's riding and travel supplications, including the return formula; Muslim, Abu Dawud, Nasa'i, and Tirmidhi transmit it through routes from Abu al-Zubayr.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p221/r2.anchor: حديث عبد الله بن عمر، رضي الله عنهما

BURSEVI:v8p272#4/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p272#4/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p272#4/r1.claim: The return to God is through death; the bier is the final worldly mount.
BURSEVI:v8p272#4/r1.anchor: {وإنا إلى ربنا لمنقلبون} ؛ أي : راجعون بالموت.

BURSEVI:v8p272#4/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p272#4/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p272#4/r2.claim: Riding should prompt reflection on the greater journey back to God, shape conduct, and serve legitimate aims such as pilgrimage, kinship, or seeking knowledge.
BURSEVI:v8p272#4/r2.anchor: وفيه إيذان بأن حق الراكب أن يتأمل فيما يلابسه من المسير ، ويتذكر منه المسافرة العظمى التي هي الانقلاب إلى الله

BURSEVI:v8p272#4/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p272#4/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p272#4/r3.claim: Because animals may stumble or bolt and ships break or sink, travelers should remember God and prepare to meet Him; death is near and each breath may be the last.
BURSEVI:v8p272#4/r3.anchor: موقع في الخطر والخوف من حيث أن راكب الدابة لا يأمن من عثارها أو شموسها مثلا

BURSEVI:v8p272#4/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p272#4/r4.speaker: قال بعضهم
BURSEVI:v8p272#4/r4.claim: Some say God's greatest gift is empowering people to master the commanding self through spiritual struggle until it obeys; gratitude follows, and once obedient it is subdued by God.
BURSEVI:v8p272#4/r4.anchor: قال بعضهم : أجل نعمة الله على العباد أن يقويهم على نفوسهم الأمارة وينصرهم عليها

BURSEVI:v8p272#4/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p272#4/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p272#4/r5.claim: Returning the self to God comes after it is subdued; recognizing divine gifts only in food, drink, and transport underestimates them.
BURSEVI:v8p272#4/r5.anchor: ومن لم يعرف نعم الله عليه إلا في مطعمه ومشربه ومركبه فقد صغر نعم الله عليه

BURSEVI:v8p272#4/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p272#4/r6.speaker: قال بعضهم
BURSEVI:v8p272#4/r6.claim: Another says return mirrors first creation: spirits came into the world, then divine attraction carries them back through the soul's mount and heart's vessel to the realm of lordship.
BURSEVI:v8p272#4/r6.anchor: وقال بعضهم : وإنا إلى ربنا لمنقلبون كما جئنا أول مرة. كما قال : {كما بدأنآ أول خلق نعيده} (الأنبياء : 104)

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r5.claim: The Prophet said In God’s name when putting a foot in the stirrup, then praised God and recited through we shall return after mounting, adding three takbīrs and three declarations of oneness.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r5.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r13.claim: Riding is dangerous: falls, runaway animals, or shipwreck may cause death, so riders should remember their certain return and prepare through reform.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r13.anchor: فلما كان الركوب مباشرة أمر مخطر ، واتصالا بسبب من أسباب التلف

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r14.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r14.claim: He warns against pleasure rides with wine and instruments, where riders remember Satan and obey him instead of preparing for death.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r14.anchor: أواني الخمر والمعازف ، فلا يزالون يسقون حتى تميل طلاهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r15.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r15.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r15.claim: He reports hearing of a ruler who drank throughout a month-long journey and only became sober after reaching his destination, unaware of the trip.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r15.anchor: وقد بلغني أن بعض السلاطين ركب وهو يشرب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r16.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r16.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r16.claim: Another reported interpretation is that riders remember mounting the funeral bier.

MUJAHID:v2p579#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p579#3/r1.speaker: إبراهيم
MUJAHID:v2p579#3/r1.claim: Ibrahim reports that ʿAlqama ibn Qays said Bismillah before mounting, praised God once seated, and recited the riding supplication when the animal rose.
MUJAHID:v2p579#3/r1.anchor: عن إبراهيم قال وضع علقمة بن قيس رجله في الغرز فقال بسم الله فلما قعد على ظهرها قال الحمد لله فلما نهض قال

MUQATIL:43:14-18/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:43:14-18/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:43:14-18/r1.claim: People will return to their Lord.
MUQATIL:43:14-18/r1.anchor: وإنا إلى ربنا لمنقلبون } [آية: 14]، يعني لراجعون

NASAFI-FULL:v4p110#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p110#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p110#3/r1.claim: The phrase means that people will return to God in the Hereafter.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p110#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p110#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p110#3/r2.claim: Some say riders recall that their final conveyance in worldly life is the bier.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p110#3/r2.anchor: قيل يذكرون عند ركوبهم مراكب الدنيا آخر مركبهم منها هو الجنازة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p110#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p110#3/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
NASAFI-FULL:v4p110#3/r3.claim: The Prophet's travel prayer begins when he puts a foot in the stirrup and continues after mounting through the words of return to God; he then says takbīr three times and tahlīl three times. For a ship, he recited the Qur'anic prayer bismillāhi majrāhā wa mursāhā, inna rabbī la-ghafūrun raḥīm.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p110#3/r3.anchor: وعن النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم إنه كان إذا وضع رجله في الركاب قال بسم الله فإذا استوى على الدابة قال الحمد لله

NASAFI-FULL:v4p110#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p110#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p110#3/r5.claim: A thoughtful person should ride for reflection rather than pleasure, considering certain death, return to God, and inability to escape His decree.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p110#3/r5.anchor: وينبغى أن لا يكون ركوب العاقل للتنزه والتلذذ بل للاعتبار

QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r6.claim: Since riding exposes people to danger, they should remember that death is certain and return to God, prepare by reforming themselves, and remain alert to a fatal accident.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r6.anchor: فلما كان الركوب مباشرة أمر محظور واتصالا بأسباب من أسباب التلف أمر ألا ينسى عند اتصاله به يومه

QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r9.claim: Uttering the formula aloud is not obligatory, but a rider should remember it when mounting, especially on a journey, and add the travel supplication asking God for company and protection from travel hardship and a bad return.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r9.anchor: وما ينبغي لعبد أن يدع قول هذا وليس بواجب ذكره باللسان فيقول متى ركب وخاصة في السفر

QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r10.claim: The supplication's phrase al-jawr ba'd al-kawr means a person's affairs becoming scattered after being in order.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r10.anchor: يعني ب «الجور بعد الكور» تشتت أمر الرجل بعد اجتماعه

QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14#2/r2.speaker: علي بن ربيعة
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14#2/r2.claim: Ali ibn Rabi'a witnessed Ali ibn Abi Talib say the riding formula and a prayer for forgiveness after mounting; Ali said he had seen the Prophet do and say the same, and the Prophet marvelled that the servant knew only God forgives sins. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi and Ibn Khuwayzimindad transmit it.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14#2/r2.anchor: وقال علي بن ربيعة: شهدت علي بن أبي طالب ركب دابة يوما فلما وضع رجله في الركاب قال: باسم الله

QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14#2/r3.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14#2/r3.claim: Al-Thalabi gives a concise version from Ali: the Prophet said bismillah when placing his foot in the stirrup and praised God on mounting, then taught a supplication on disembarking from a ship or animal.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14#2/r3.anchor: وذكر الثعلبي نحوه مختصرا عن علي رضي الله عنه، ولفظه عنه

RAZI-FULL:v27p172/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p172/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p172/r1.claim: Riding ships and animals exposes their riders to death; the verse therefore links riding to remembering inevitable death and readiness to return to God.
RAZI-FULL:v27p172/r1.anchor: واعلم أن وجه اتصال هذا الكلام بما قبله أن ركوب الفلك في خطر الهلاك ، فإنه كثيرا ما تنكسر السفينة

STUDYQURAN:43:14/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:14/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:43:14/r1.claim: The phrase may mean that people turn to their Lord in prayer, or alternatively that they return to Him in the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:43:14/r1.anchor: that is, in prayer. Alternately, the phrase could be rendered, “Unto our Lord do we return” in the Hereafter (Aj, IK,R, Ṭ).

STUDYQURAN:43:14/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:14/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:43:14/r2.claim: On the Hereafter reading, earthly journeys recall the journey to the Hereafter, and travel provisions recall the need to prepare with reverence.
STUDYQURAN:43:14/r2.anchor: mention of earthly journeys in the previous verse draws one’s attention to the journey toward the Hereafter

STUDYQURAN:43:14/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:14/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:43:14/r3.claim: The return after mentioning travel recognizes the dangers of setting out unprepared and that successful return depends entirely on God.
STUDYQURAN:43:14/r3.anchor: recognition of the dangers inherent in setting out upon a journey, especially without the necessary preparation, and that the successful return from a journey lies entirely in God’s Hands

STUDYQURAN:43:14/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:14/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:43:14/r4.claim: The active participle munqalibūn makes the return definitive: all people travel toward God at every moment, whether willingly or not.
STUDYQURAN:43:14/r4.anchor: “are we returners”) speaks to the definitive nature of this verse

TAB-FULL:v20p557/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p557/r2.speaker: أبو مجلز
TAB-FULL:v20p557/r2.claim: Abū Majliz recounts that a rider, identified by Sufyān as al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, told him to praise Allah for Islam, Muhammad, and being the best community before reciting the riding formula.
TAB-FULL:v20p557/r2.anchor: عن أبي مجلز قال: ركبت دابة، فقلت: {سبحان الذي سخر لنا هذا

TAB-FULL:v20p557/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p557/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v20p557/r3.claim: Qatāda says to say the basmala when boarding ships, the glorification formula when riding camels, and a prayer asking for a blessed landing when disembarking.
TAB-FULL:v20p557/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، {لتستووا على ظهوره ثم تذكروا نعمة ربكم إذا استويتم عليه} [الزخرف: 13] " يعلمكم كيف تقولون إذا ركبتم في الفلك تقولون

TAB-FULL:v20p557/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p557/r4.speaker: طاوس
TAB-FULL:v20p557/r4.claim: Ṭāwūs would say that the ride was from Allah’s favor and grace, then recite the glorification formula.
TAB-FULL:v20p557/r4.anchor: عن ابن طاوس، عن أبيه، أنه كان إذا ركب قال

TABATABAI:43:13-14/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:43:13-14/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:43:13-14/r7.claim: The declaration that they will return to their Lord affirms resurrection.

TABRISI:43:11-14/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:43:11-14/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:43:11-14/r13.claim: Riders also say they return to God at life's end on another conveyance, the funeral bier.
TABRISI:43:11-14/r13.anchor: في آخر عمرنا على مركب آخر وهو الجنازة

THALABI:v8p329/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p329/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p329/r2.claim: Munqalibūn means that people will return to God at the Resurrection.
THALABI:v8p329/r2.anchor: وإنا إلى ربنا لمنقلبون لمنصرفون في المعاد.

THALABI:v8p329/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p329/r3.speaker: علي
THALABI:v8p329/r3.claim: Ali reports that the Prophet said bismillah when placing his foot in the stirrup, then on mounting praised God, recited these verses, and repeated takbīr and tahlīl three times each. No grading is stated.
THALABI:v8p329/r3.anchor: عن علي رضي الله عنه، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، إنه كان إذا وضع رجله في الركاب،

THALABI:v8p329/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p329/r4.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v8p329/r4.claim: Qatada says the verse teaches what to say when riding ships or livestock and cites the prayer for a blessed landing from 23:29.
THALABI:v8p329/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة: في هذه الآية يعلمكم كيف تقولون إذا ركبتم في الفلك والأنعام تقولون:

ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r17.speaker: Resûl-i Ekrem
ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r17.claim: A report says the Prophet said the basmala at the stirrup, praised God when mounted, recited the cited glorification and return verse, then said three takbīrs and three tahlīls.
ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r17.anchor: Rivayet olunur ki Resûl-i Ekrem sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem ayağını üzengiye koyduğu zaman بِسْمِ اللهِّٰ der, hayvanın üzerine doğrulduğunda اَلْحَمْدُ لِلهِ عَلَى كُ ِّل حَالٍ.

ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r19.claim: All our changes and journeys lead toward God, and ultimately we arrive at Him; the verse expresses Islam’s greatest aim, spirit, and consolation, echoing the return to God (2:156).
ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r19.anchor: bütün inkılâbâtımız, dönüp dolaşmamız O’na doğrudur, nihâyet O’na varacağız. Bu âyet de إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّآ إِلَيْهِ رَٰجِعُونَ mazmûnu üzere İslâm’ın en büyük gayesini

ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r20.claim: A rider should see a journey as a change of state that prompts reflection on the greater journey to God, and therefore ride only for a licit purpose.
ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r20.anchor: bir inkılab olduğunu düşünmeli, ondan da asıl büyük yolculuğu, Allah’a olan seyr ü inkılâbı düşünmeli de o mülâhazaya göre hareket etmeli.
